interface.title: SeismicLens v2.0 — Interactive Seismic Waveform Analyzer
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis and teaching: generate or load one waveform, filter it, look at its spectra, pick a phase, export the results
interface.what_it_is_for: Generate a synthetic earthquake seismogram or load a single waveform, then bandpass filter it, run FFT/PSD/spectrogram analysis and an STA/LTA P-wave pick, and export each result as CSV.

data.note: Mainly the built-in synthetic earthquake generator (the default). Both test files were also uploaded: waveform_time_amplitude.csv (60 samples; sample rate inferred as 50 Hz; 1.2 s long) and waveform_single_column.csv (80 samples; 100 Hz assumed; 0.8 s long). In the two-column file, the blank amplitude at t=0.60 s became a 0 rather than being interpolated, so a notch shows in the raw and filtered trace (screens/042.webp). MiniSEED upload was opened, but there was no MiniSEED test file. INGV/IRIS Live was not used, as instructed.

features.name: Synthetic event generator with summary metrics and ground-truth metadata
features.general: Set a few physical source parameters with sliders, get a simulated time series at once, and compare headline metrics with the hidden true values shown in a JSON panel
features.specific: Sliders for magnitude, focal depth, epicentral distance, noise and duration produce an IASP91-like seismogram. The metric cards show fs, duration, peak amplitude and dominant frequency, plus P Arrival and S–P Delay cards; these two come from the STA/LTA pick (P Arrival = detector pick, S–P = true S arrival minus that pick), not from the synthetic ground truth. The 'Trace / Synthetic metadata' expander lists the true p_arrival, s_arrival, sp_delay and surface-wave time.
steps: Choose 'Synthetic earthquake' as data source
Move the magnitude, depth, distance, noise and duration sliders
Read the metric cards (peak amplitude, dominant frequency, and the detector-based P arrival and S–P delay)
Expand the metadata panel to see the true arrival times and compare
serves_tasks: Simulate a signal from physical source parameters and inspect it
Tune an automatic event detector and read the first trigger time

features.name: Bandpass filter with raw-overlay comparison
features.general: Set a frequency band and filter order, apply a zero-phase filter, and compare the filtered trace with the original either overlaid or by switching the filter off
features.specific: In the Butterworth Filter section, set Low cut and High cut sliders and choose Order (2/4/6/8). The 'Zero-phase bandpass' switch turns the filter on or off, and 'Raw signal overlay' draws the raw trace in grey under the filtered one. Badges above the plot and a details card report the band, effective order, Nyquist frequency and roll-off.
steps: Set Low cut and High cut sliders
Choose filter order from the dropdown
Switch on 'Raw signal overlay' to see the raw trace under the filtered one
Switch the 'Zero-phase bandpass' off and on to compare filtered and unfiltered
Read the band, order, Nyquist and roll-off from the badges and details card
serves_tasks: Keep only a chosen frequency band, compare it with the unfiltered signal, and zoom in where needed

features.name: Time-series plot with event markers, box zoom and reset
features.general: An interactive trace plot with vertical markers for detected or expected events, drag-to-zoom on a region, hover readout of values, and one-click reset
features.specific: Plotly 'Seismic Waveform (filtered/unfiltered)' chart with dashed P and S markers. You can box-zoom on the P onset, hover for (time, amplitude), and use the toolbar to reset axes, pan or download a PNG.
steps: Drag a box over the region of interest to zoom
Hover a point to read time and amplitude
Press Reset axes to return to the full view
serves_tasks: Keep only a chosen frequency band, compare it with the unfiltered signal, and zoom in where needed

features.name: Spectrum panel with peak/centroid/bandwidth metrics and optional phase and PSD views
features.general: Compute an amplitude spectrum, mark its peak and centroid, report spread and frequency resolution, and add or remove companion views (phase, averaged power density)
features.specific: The Spectral Analysis tab shows Dominant Freq, Spectral Centroid and RMS Bandwidth cards plus a frequency-resolution card (df = fs/N). It has an FFT amplitude spectrum with Peak and Centroid lines, an optional FFT phase spectrum and an optional Welch PSD in dB. The last two are controlled by Display Options switches.
steps: Open the Spectral Analysis tab
Read dominant frequency, centroid, bandwidth and df
Inspect the FFT amplitude spectrum with its Peak and Centroid markers
Switch on Phase spectrum and/or Power Spectral Density to add those charts
serves_tasks: Find the main frequency, mean frequency and spread of the signal

features.name: Time–frequency heatmap with hover and zoom
features.general: Show signal energy over time and frequency as a heatmap, read cell values on hover, and zoom into a band and time window
features.specific: STFT spectrogram (dB colour scale) where the P pulse (~10 Hz) and S pulse (~4 Hz) appear as distinct bright patches, with a bright low-frequency band near 0–1 Hz. Hover shows x (s), y (Hz) and z (dB). Box zoom isolates 0–15 Hz.
steps: Open the Spectrogram tab
Hover a bright patch to read time, frequency and dB
Drag a box to zoom into a frequency band and time window
serves_tasks: See how frequency content changes over time

features.name: STA/LTA trigger tuner
features.general: Tune the two averaging windows and the threshold of a ratio-based onset detector, and see the ratio curve, shaded trigger windows and first-trigger time update
features.specific: Sidebar STA window, LTA window and Trigger threshold sliders drive the 'STA/LTA Characteristic Function' plot (with threshold line and shaded trigger windows). They also update the 'First trigger … · Total trigger windows' message, the summary cards (STA, LTA, LTA/STA, threshold) and the P-arrival marker on the Waveform tab.
steps: Open the STA/LTA tab and read the first trigger time
Change the LTA window
Change the trigger threshold (the threshold line moves)
Change the STA window
Read the new first trigger, the trigger-window count and the updated P Arrival / S–P cards
serves_tasks: Tune an automatic event detector and read the first trigger time

features.name: Table upload with sampling-rate inference
features.general: Upload a one- or two-column table as a time series; the tool infers or assumes the sampling rate and reports sample count and duration
features.specific: The 'Upload CSV' source takes amplitude-only files (fs assumed 100 Hz) or time,amplitude files (fs inferred from the time column). The metadata panel shows source, n_samples, sampling_rate_hz and duration_s, and the x button clears the file.
steps: Choose 'Upload CSV' as data source
Press Upload and pick a CSV file
Check fs, N and duration in the metric cards and metadata panel
Remove the file with x and upload another
serves_tasks: Load your own measured signal from a table file

features.name: Multi-product CSV export with preview
features.general: Download each computed result (processed series, spectrum, power density, detector curve) as its own CSV, preview the first rows, and get starter code to reload them
features.specific: The Export tab has Download signal / FFT / PSD / STA/LTA CSV buttons, a 'Signal preview (first 200 samples)' table, and a 'Python code examples' expander with pandas/matplotlib snippets.
steps: Open the Export tab
Press each Download button
Check the signal preview table
Expand the Python code examples
serves_tasks: Download the processed signal and derived spectra and detector output as tables

features.name: S–P delay to epicentral distance readout (Wadati)
features.general: Turn the time between the first and second wave arrivals into an estimate of distance to the source, and compare it with the known distance of a simulated event
features.specific: Under the waveform plot the app prints the synthetic S arrival, the S–P delay and an epicentral distance by the Wadati method. The P time is the STA/LTA pick, so the distance inherits its error: at default settings (true P 12.21 s, pick 20.00 s) it reads S–P 1.36 s and about 10.9 km against the true 80 km set on the distance slider.
steps: Generate a synthetic event with a known epicentral distance
Scroll below the waveform plot to the S arrival / S–P delay / Wadati distance readout
Compare the estimated distance with the distance slider and the true arrivals in the metadata panel
serves_tasks: Estimate distance to the source from the S–P time
Tune an automatic event detector and read the first trigger time

features.name: Reference layered velocity model
features.general: Look up the layered material properties behind a simulation as a table and a chart, with short explanations of the derived quantities
features.specific: The Velocity Model tab shows an IASP91-like four-layer crustal table (depth, Vp, Vs, Vp/Vs, Poisson ratio, density), a grouped bar chart of Vp and Vs per layer, and explanation cards with the Vp/Vs and Poisson formulas.
steps: Open the Velocity Model tab
Read the layer table
Read the Vp and Vs grouped bar chart
Scroll to the explanation cards and formulas
serves_tasks: Look up the layered material model used for the simulation
